files.author: Beyond My Ken
files.caption: The Stone Arch Bridge, located near the intersection East Springfield Avenue and South Second Street in Champaign, Illinois was built in 1860. In c.2010, it was integrated into the design of the Boneyard Creek Second Street Basin, a flood control facility and recreational amenity which is located between First and Second Streets and Springfield and University Avenues.(SourceL [1])

files.author: Smallbones
files.caption: Stone Arch Bridge on the NRHP since May 14, 1981. At NW corner of Springfield Ave. and 2nd St., Champaign, Champaign County, Illinois. Underwent reconstruction and/or destruction over the last 2 years.  Very strange story, according to my understanding.  "Bridge" was built in the 1870s but was more like a culvert or a pipe, 10 feet long by 100 feet wide, eventually turning the Boneyard Creek into an underground waterway at this point.
